title: Data Flow Explorer
description: A spoken question travels through eight hops, from the microphone to the device status the broker keeps. At each hop someone can see the data, and two design choices change who: turning network encryption off exposes the network hops to anyone on the Wi-Fi, and moving speech-to-text, the agent and text-to-speech to an outside vendor gives that vendor the question and the reply.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Study Buddy
Privacy, Safety, and Responsible Listening
Data Flow
Hop
Observer
Network Encryption
Local Versus Cloud Processing

learningObjectives: The learner will examine the 8 hops of a spoken question under two settings (network encryption on or off, services on the school server or at an outside vendor) and count how many hops each observer can see, answering 6 what-if questions with at least 5 of 6 correct.
prerequisites: hop, observer, network encryption, school server, outside vendor, broker (all defined in the sections above this block; the broker is defined in Chapter 15 and named in the hop table).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Is data that stays on the Wi-Fi private?
What does moving the services to a vendor change about who sees the audio?
Is only the audio sensitive, or the text too?
commonMisconceptions: (1) Only the person who owns the device can see what they say. (2) If the data stays on the Wi-Fi it is private. (3) Moving the services to a vendor changes nothing about who sees the audio. (4) Only the audio is sensitive, not the text.
assessmentOpportunities: Answer all six questions. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
